facts.raw_span: 2-week history of vegetating, bleeding plaques and pustules on his face, scalp, trunk, and extremities
Lesions began as pustules and developed into painful, itchy plaques
Pustules and hemorrhagic-crusted plaques were seen on the scalp, legs, arms, and trunk along with keloidal plaques on the face
difficulty walking due to skin lesions
Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay testing for HIV was negative
Punch biopsy from arm showed: Epidermal hyperplasia and exocytosis of neutrophils
Dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration
Microabscesses scattered with eosinophils
No granulomas or multinucleated giant cells
Negative periodic acid–Schiff staining
Extensive vegetative plaques with bleeding and ulceration
Pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia (hematoxylin-eosin stain)

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques and pustules, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia, dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, and microabscesses, is consistent with Pyoderma Gangrenosum.
The patient's symptoms and histopathological findings, including the presence of dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration and microabscesses, are also consistent with Sweet Syndrome.

Although the patient's HIV test was negative, the presence of extensive vegetative plaques with bleeding and ulceration, along with the negative periodic acid-Schiff staining, could suggest Eczema Herpeticum, especially if the patient has a history of atopic dermatitis.
The patient's presentation of pustules and hemorrhagic-crusted plaques, along with the negative periodic acid-Schiff staining, could also suggest Impetigo, a bacterial skin infection.

The patient's symptoms, including the presence of painful, itchy plaques, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia and dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, could also suggest Psoriasis.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques and pustules, along with the negative periodic acid-Schiff staining, could suggest Dermatitis Herpetiformis, a skin condition associated with celiac disease.

The patient's symptoms, including the presence of itchy plaques, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia and dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, could also suggest Seborrheic Dermatitis.

The patient's presentation of painful, itchy plaques and pustules, along with the histopathological findings of epidermal hyperplasia and dense dermal-mixed inflammatory cell infiltration, could also suggest Pityriasis Rubra Pilaris.

The patient's presentation of pustules and hemorrhagic-crusted plaques, along with the histopathologic findings of epidermal hyperplasia, exocytosis of neutrophils, and microabscesses with eosinophils, is consistent with Acute Generalized Exanthematous Pustulosis, which is often triggered by medications or infections, and the negative HIV test helps to rule out other conditions.
